drivers.summary: Anglo-French competition in India becomes structurally asymmetric.
Revolutionary/Napoleonic war transfers Dutch Ceylon to Britain before 1815.

amplifiers.summary: Reduced Dutch/French alternatives narrow Kandyan balancing options.

consequences.summary: Internal Kandyan fracture becomes unusually exploitable.

protagonists.name: East India Company / Britain
protagonists.objective: Remove rival strategic positions and secure Ceylon.

what_changed: Britain becomes the dominant European regional military framework around Ceylon.
1815 occurs inside a much narrower balancing environment.

prepares_next.bullet: British rule inherits and expands administrative legibility while local social hierarchies continue to shape access and labour.
